Treatment summary
Patient presented following a sideswipe collision that occurred during a lane change. The patient reports low back
pain with stiffness and muscle tightness across the lumbar region. Over the course of eight visits, care consisted of
manual therapy, guided stretching, and a home exercise program. Palpation revealed paraspinal muscle tenderness
and reduced range of motion in forward flexion, consistent with a soft tissue strain. Neurological screening, including
reflexes and sensation in the lower extremities, was within normal limits. Straight leg raise testing was negative. The
reported severity of symptoms is considerably greater than what would ordinarily be expected from the mechanism
described, and the course of treatment extended somewhat beyond the typical timeframe for a lumbar strain of this
kind. The patient reports no prior injury or treatment involving the lower back. Billing records reviewed for this episode
of care show no duplicate or repeated charges. Ongoing management includes continued home exercise and
reassessment at follow-up.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
